set.approach: Take the Convict Lake trail and scree slope up into the hanging valley below the north face, then keep going up the valley almost to the low point on the skyline that divides Mount Morrison from Mini Morrison. The gully is a conspicuous deep red gash at the far end of the northeast shoulder and stays in view all the way up the valley.
set.descent_text: The route finishes at the east ridge, on the northeast shoulder, with an easy snow gully leading about 800 feet on to the summit. One option is to go on to the summit and walk down the east slopes. The other is to cut south over a rock buttress, which has no technical difficulty, and then drop onto the east slope. Do not drop into the prominent gully right under the finish, because it ends in cliffs.

set.approach: Take the Convict Lake trail and scree slope up into the hanging valley below the north face. The start is in the back corner of the northwest shoulder, between the north buttress and the subpeak Torre De Mierda, about 300 feet right of Deception and shared with Learning to Walk. The first pitch climbs the buttress on the left side of the couloir dividing Torre De Mierda from the main peak.
set.descent_text: The route ends on the Northwest Ridge. Either follow the ridge to the summit and descend the east face, or skip the summit: go down the ridge over loose third-class ground to a large open couloir on the north (skier's right) side, then descend very loose talus or snow.

set.approach: From the Convict Lake parking lot on the lake's east side, take the trail toward the south end of the lake, then leave it and grind up the scree hillside to the hanging valley below the north face. In winter this is the better way in. The couloir is easy to pick out to the right of the north buttress, and it is a funnel for rockfall.
set.descent_text: Walk off down the east slopes of the peak. Do not go back down the couloir itself, because rockfall there is serious.

set.approach: Take the Convict Lake trail and scree slope up into the hanging valley below the north face, then keep going up the valley almost to the low point on the skyline that divides Mount Morrison from Mini Morrison. The deep red gash of Caught Inside is easy to see, and Psychopomp starts a little to its left.
set.descent_text: The climbing ends on a ridge on the northeast shoulder, with easy snow leading about 800 feet on to the summit. One option is to go on to the summit and walk down the east slopes. The other is to cut south over a rock buttress, which has no technical difficulty, and then drop onto the east slope. Do not drop into the prominent gully right under the finish, because it ends in cliffs.

set.approach: Start at the Saddlebag Lake trailhead, drop below the dam and cross the stream, then follow the west shore of the lake, passing Greenstone Lake on its north side. Continue along a shallow slot valley beyond Wasco Lake, leave the main trail to the left and go round the east and north shores of Cascade Lake. A climbers' trail climbs the rocky, grassy slope on Cascade Lake's north side to a shelf and talus field. Turn left and head south to the foot of the North Peak snowfield, and climb it to the couloir.
set.descent_text: The ice ends at a notch. From there a low fifth-class scramble to climbers' right reaches the summit, or you can descend south toward Conness Lake.

set.approach: Drive to the Sherwin Lakes and Valentine Lake trailhead and follow the trail past Sherwin Lakes toward Valentine Lake. Opposite the peak, cross a long talus field to the base. Snow over the talus makes it easier in winter and spring, and skis can be used. The route is the only other full-length snow couloir left of the central couloir that splits the face.
set.descent_text: The route reaches the southeastern summit of Pyramid Peak. Head southeast over moderate snow, then retrace the approach.

set.approach: Start at Lake Wit-So-Nah-Pah and walk up to Constance Lake, then climb a moraine to the glacier at the foot of the couloir. Rockfall is a serious hazard here.
set.descent_text: Head northwest over scree slopes to a saddle, then go north back down to Lake Wit-So-Nah-Pah.

set.descent_text: Hike off to the right around the rocks. If thawing, trees farther back can be used for a top-rope anchor.

set.approach: The runnel is on the south side of the highway near the Deadman curves, in the largest volcanic opening on that side. Park at the pullout skiers use for the snow bridge, cross the creek where it is safe, and skin, ski or hike up to the first tier. If the first tier has no snow, a trail to the east (used for Blue Canyon) gives access from the side.

set.approach: From the Red Lakes trailhead, the trail starts a little north of Red Mountain Creek and switchbacks uphill, then turns west and runs above the creek to Red Lake and the foot of Split Mountain. The couloir starts a long way up the slope above Red Lake. The couloir is a funnel for rockfall.

Turn up the third wash, the most prominent drainage off the south side of Tahquitz, and follow it to the large slab that holds the flow.

set.descent_text: Two ways off: the snowfield below the fire lookout, which takes more effort, or the Altar Couloir, which is more technical.

set.approach: Start from the Lodgepole visitor center and market parking lot, go over the bridge on its east side, and take the Tokopah Valley Trail to the right. The route is down-canyon (west) from Moonage Daydream.
set.descent_text: Rappel on V-threads from the top of the third pitch, or continue up the slabs above the ice.

set.approach: Start from the Lodgepole visitor center and market parking lot, go over the bridge on its east side, and take the Tokopah Valley Trail to the right. Follow it until the Watchtower appears on the canyon's south side; the ice fills a clear gully on that wall's north flank. Avalanche terrain lies above the climb, so check the avalanche forecast.

set.approach: The route is on the far right side of the Watchtower, above Hoppy's Favorite. From the top of that ice, climb steep snow through the trees to the base of the first obstacle on the route.

set.approach: The falls are a common hike out of Lodgepole: walk beside the stream, cross a bridge a short way along, and keep going up-canyon to the falls. Where the trail stops, scramble down and cross snow bridges to get to the ice. Check the avalanche forecast for the slopes above.
set.descent_text: Walk off to the west, or rappel from trees.

set.approach: Hike the Whitney Trail until it forks right onto the North Fork Trail toward the Lower and Upper Boy Scout Lakes. The flows form on slabs to the left, and are visible from the lower lake when present. Cross the talus between the two lakes and choose a line up to the ice. Snowshoes can help. Mount Whitney zone permit rules apply.
set.descent_text: Walk off to climber's right, or rappel using V-threads or the anchors on the left side of the flow. Two ropes are needed unless you walk off.
